The colour green and red of the female representatives of the genus Falsomordellistena resemble those of the airborne flower of the small bee, and are both clear-headed and tutus (bright-eyed heads). On the thorax, both species are *penetrating, i.e. the head is pointed inwards at the intersection of two color lines, while on the abdomen they are longer pointed upwards. Some students think that an online course is cyber-surfing
text:

However, studying online can be extremely difficult, since most users only have their phone number and all their information put into the program. Some students also prefer to study online by using that course. In one study published in the Journal of Higher Education, 126 college students in four different classes stated they had found it difficult to learn if they had no contact information. Another study showed that there was a slightly higher chance of choosing an online course than the Internet because students would have less of an understanding of the content. The great thing is that most of the students returned to school with positive feelings about their learning.

prefix: Hincks Wilderness Protection Area is a protected area in the Australian state of South Australia
text:
, where the largest north-south road in Australia is the Kempsey Coastal Road. Due to the proximity to the mainland to the south, Hincks Wilderness Protection Area includes the northern part of the Yuat River.

Coastal animals are widely present in Hincks Wilderness; the South Australia Game and Plants (NASAGPA) and University of South Australia red-tailed lizards are highly prevalent in the area. Other species in the area are wild foxes, rabbits, dogs, birds and the Palpite version of a social butterfly that feeds on "killables".
